svg.title: How the Uqda network works
svg.desc: Uqda is an encrypted IPv6 overlay network built only from its users' devices. Each device runs a node; nodes link to nearby nodes and route each other's traffic. There is no central server.
svg.text: Uqda is an encrypted IPv6 overlay network built only from its users' devices. Each device runs a
node; nodes link to nearby nodes and route each other's traffic. There is no central server.
Topology: nodes, peer links and sessions
Every box is a device running Uqda. Peer links use whatever network exists;
an encrypted session runs end to end across any number of them.
LAN peers found by multicast; works without internet
Addressing: the address is computed from the key
The public key is inverted bit by bit; its leading 1-bits are counted and dropped. Nobody can
use an address without its private key, so the source address of a packet identifies the sender.
Routed /64 subnet for devices behind the node
Programs see an ordinary IPv6 interface. Below it, Uqda filters, encrypts and routes,
then hands frames to a normal network connection.
Two nodes open a connection and prove their keys. Between Uqda nodes the proof covers fresh
random values, so a recorded handshake cannot be replayed to impersonate a node.
1. connect over TCP, TLS, QUIC or WebSocket
2. metadata: version, public key, nonce (field 0x7571), signature
3. Ed25519 signature over (B's nonce, A's nonce, both keys)
4. Ed25519 signature over (A's nonce, B's nonce, both keys)
Both signatures verify: the link is up. A replayed handshake fails, because the nonce is new on every connection.
Yggdrasil nodes and older Uqda releases skip steps 3 and 4; RequireFreshHandshake: true rejects them.
Routing: coordinates on a spanning tree
Nodes agree on a tree by gossip. A node's coordinates are its path from the root. Each hop goes
to the peer with the smallest tree distance to the destination, so extra links become shortcuts.
distance(a, b) = depth(a) + depth(b) - 2 x common_prefix(a, b)
No node stores a routing table
Finding a node: lookups and repair
The destination address holds only part of the key. A lookup travels towards nodes whose
bloom filters may contain it; the answer carries the full key and current coordinates.
forwarded only on links whose bloom filter matches
4. link fails: "path broken" back to the sender
5. A looks B up again; traffic takes the new path.
SSH from the laptop to the friend's PC. Relays carry ciphertext they cannot read or change.
Relays see the keys in the routing header, size and timing.
They cannot read, modify or replay the content.
9. reply on the same flow, allowed back automatically
Uqda encrypts content end to end. It does not hide that you use it, or whom you talk to.
¹ Only on plain TCP links. TLS and QUIC links hide it from your provider.
² Unless that node is also one of your direct peers. Uqda has no telemetry: nothing is sent to its developers.
Both use the same overlay and the same relays. A group secret limits who can open a session.
Any node can open a session with yours.
The firewall decides what it may reach.
Only members can open sessions. Other nodes
Applied to traffic that arrives over Uqda, before it reaches your programs. On for new nodes.
reply to a flow this node opened
1. part of a flow this node opened: allow
Joining a private group with an invite
The invite is a one-time code without a password. The group secret is sent only to a device
that reaches the inviter over TLS 1.3 pinned to the inviter's key and presents the code's secret.
uqda setup: key pair, group secret
token: inviter key, up to 4 addresses,
1. token shown as text and QR code; the user copies it
2. TLS 1.3 to an address in the token; certificate key must equal token key
after a restart it is a member
Anything that listens on IPv6 works unchanged. The source address of a connection is authenticated.
Host a site or service at home, without port forwarding.
Use the client's 200:… address as its login.
Read node state through the local admin API (JSON).
Embed a node in apps with the Android and Apple SDKs.
# any Uqda user can now open
Not an anonymity network: peers see your IP address, relays see who talks to whom.
Experimental: tested extensively, but no independent security audit yet.
Paths can be longer than a direct connection, so some routes are slower.
No telemetry, no accounts, no central servers.
